eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in short-range forecasts for Kuala Lumpur's May 16 high temperature, with implied probabilities clustered around 31–33°C due to varying model outputs from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and global ensembles. MetMalaysia's latest advisory projects a 34°C maximum amid isolated afternoon thunderstorms, but aggregators like timeanddate indicate ~32°C peaks under overcast skies and 60%+ storm risk, potentially capping heating via convective cloud cover before 2–4 p.m. local time. Equatorial diurnal patterns, consistent May climatology averaging 32°C highs, and urban heat island effects differentiate outcomes, with earlier storms favoring 31°C and delayed activity enabling 33°C+. New MetMalaysia and ECMWF/GFS updates expected overnight could sharpen odds ahead of resolution.
